newsitem.title: GERMANY: Berlin property values drop after post-unity surge.
newsitem.headline: Berlin property values drop after post-unity surge.

text.p: Property values in west Berlin plunged by up to 20 percent in 1996 while prices in the eastern half of the formerly divided city held steady last year, construction senator Juergen Klemann said on Friday.
Real estate values quickly multiplied in the months after the Berlin Wall fell in 1989 and German reunified in 1990, but stagnated for several years before softening in the mid-1990s.
"This is a return to normalcy," Klemann said at a news conference. The steepest declines were recorded in the leafy sections of west Berlin such as Grunewald and Dahlem.

He said he hoped the lower prices would slow the exodus from the city of families, who have been moving outside the city in recent years to less expensive housing in the newly opened suburbs around the city.
Klemann said the decline in the west and steady prices in the east made property values comparable for the first time in decades. He said prices could continue falling slightly this year.
